It helps to look at some history leading up to the attack.

In 1940 Japan invaded French Indochina which prompted the US to place an embargo on all oil exports to Japan. At the time Japan imported 80% of its oil from the US. The Japanese navy estimated they had 2 years of stockpiled oil. To solve this problem the Japanese war planners then looked south, especially to Brunei for oil and Malaya for rubber and tin. However they believed (probably wrongly) the US would use the Philippines (a US territory) to defend the south pacific if Japan made a move to the south.

The Japanese military concluded an invasion of the Philippines would provoke an American military response. Rather than seize and fortify the islands, and wait for the inevitable U.S. counterattack, Japan's military leaders instead decided on the preventive Pearl Harbor attack, which they assumed would negate the American forces needed for the liberation and reconquest of the islands.

Unfortunately (for them) they didn't manage to take out the entire Pacific fleet.

The short of it was, once the US placed the oil embargo Japan felt war with the US was inevitable. To them it was better to strike first than wait. The stupid thing is, if Japan had just ignored the Philippines there was a good chance the US would not have gone to war. There was little public support for it until Japan attacked Pearl Harbor (and botched their Declaration of War).
